gap: No result ChatGPT got states which add-on trigger works when the projector has no 12 V trigger output and the screen is a floor-rising Elite Kestrel. Elite's ZU12V universal trigger is 'Not compatible with Floor-Rising Up/Down Screens'. Elite's ZUSBV-RC1 USB trigger, which plugs into the projector's 5 V USB Type-A port, lists the Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR 3, the Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 CineGrey 4D and the Kestrel Tab-Tension CLR 5 as compatible, but only on RC1-version screens.
standout_why: I compared five pages. projector-screen-guide.com says the Kestrel CLR3 has a wired or wireless 12 V trigger. projectorverdict.com (motorized) says Elite SWIFT-RC1 screens support a 12 V trigger and that the Spectrum 2 needs the ZPM-RT3 kit. It also says VIVIDSTORM's trigger dongle 'does not work with every projector'. primeareviews.com mentions AWOL's USB sync but names no projectors. None of these pages names an add-on trigger for a projector without a 12 V output. None says Elite's ZU12V excludes floor-rising screens or that the ZUSBV-RC1 is the Kestrel-compatible option. All three already cover the UST versus long-throw material split, so that part is not new.
decides: This finding confirms the pick more than it changes it. Before buying a Kestrel, a shopper should check that the projector has a 12 V trigger output or a powered USB Type-A port, and that the screen is the RC1 version. Without either, the screen cannot rise and fall with the projector's power, and the discontinued ZU12V is no fallback. The throw-type split matters for the Elite and VIVIDSTORM screens below. The Kestrel TT3 CineWhite is the only one rated for UST, short throw and standard throw. The Kestrel TT3 CineGrey 4D is standard-throw only. The Kestrel CLR and CLR3 and the VIVIDSTORM S PRO and S PRO P are UST only. The VIVIDSTORM S ALR and S White Cinema are for standard throw.

findings.product: Elite Screens ZU12V universal wireless 5-12V trigger
findings.label: Floor-rising exclusion
findings.value: "Not compatible with Floor-Rising Up/Down Screens, ZZ Type or RC1 Electric Screens". Made for projectors with no low-voltage trigger port. Fits inline on the projector's power cord and runs on 110 V or 220 V.
findings.source_title: Electric Screen Accessory – Universal Wireless 5-12V Projector Trigger ZU12V (Elite Screens)
findings.note: Maker's own accessory page. Its incompatible list also includes VMAX 3, VMAX Tab-Tension 3 and CineTension 3. The page marks the product discontinued, and it contradicts itself on Version 2.0 versus 3.0 control boards.

findings.product: Elite Screens ZUSBV-RC1 wireless USB trigger
findings.label: Kestrel models listed as compatible
findings.value: Kestrel Tab-Tension CLR 5, Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 CineGrey 4D and Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR 3. Not compatible with 'All Non-RC1 versions' or any Yard Master Electric or Wireless model.
findings.source_title: Electric Screen Accessory – Wireless USB Projector Trigger ZUSBV-RC1 (Elite Screens)
findings.note: Lists copied verbatim from the maker's page. The Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 CineWhite (FTE122H3 and others) is not named in the compatible list. No price is shown on the page.

findings.label: Projector port and screen control requirement
findings.value: The ZUSBV-RC1 is 'designed for projectors with a USB Type-A power port (5V)'. The ZU12V1 is 'intended for projectors without a 12V trigger output'. 'Both wireless triggers are only compatible with Elite electric screens equipped with the RC1 control system.'
findings.source_title: Q: How do I determine if my projector is compatible with the ZU12V1 or ZUSBV-RC1 Wireless Trigger? (Elite Screens FAQ)
findings.note: This FAQ's 'RC1 only' line contradicts the ZU12V product page, which lists RC1 screens as incompatible. Either way, the ZU12V page excludes floor-rising screens.

findings.label: Projector throw compatibility and trigger
findings.value: CineWhite (1.1 gain): 'Works with Standard, Ultra/Short-throw 1080P/4K projectors', triple laser included. The CineGrey 4D version is listed for standard throw only. A 12 V trigger works wired through the wall box or wirelessly through the RF remote. Sizes: 122, 140, 150 and 183 in diagonal (FTE122H3, FTE140H3, FTE150H3, FTE183H3).
findings.source_title: Electric Floor-Rising Projection Screen – Kestrel Tab-Tension 3 (Elite Screens)
findings.note: Maker's product page. The 122 in CineWhite is the 'Kestrel Tab-Tension3, 122"' that ChatGPT showed for $1,923. It is the only floor-rising screen found here rated for both UST and standard throw.

findings.product: Elite Screens Kestrel Tab-Tension CLR (FTE101UH-CLR / FTE121UH-CLR)
findings.label: Throw exclusion
findings.value: 'Not Compatible With Short or Standard Throw Projectors'. The material 'requires a minimum projector lens throw ratio 0.3x the image width'. Built-in IR and RF receivers. Sizes: 101 in and 121 in, 16:9.
findings.source_title: Motorized CLR Floor-Rising Projection Screen – Kestrel Tab-Tension CLR (Elite Screens)
